# LVGL to ferrovgl mapping

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask gen-mapping` from the LVGL v9.6.0 headers and the ferrovgl doc comments. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Overall: 1519/2899 upstream public functions and aliases (233 deprecated aliases) mapped (52.4%); 7 crate-internal, 711 excluded, 662 not ported.**

## Using the Rust API

ferrovgl keeps the names, numeric values and behaviour of LVGL v9.6.0, so
the upstream documentation applies; only ownership is redesigned
(`docs/PLAN.md` 4.1).

- **One context.** `lv_init()` is `Ui::new(UiConfig::default())`. The `Ui`
  owns every object, display, input device, group, timer, animation, shared
  style and event callback; there is no global state. The software renderer
  is registered with `ferrovgl_draw_sw::init(&mut ui)` right after
  `Ui::new`. The main loop is the C one: `ui.tick_inc(ms)` and
  `ui.timer_handler()`.
- **Handles.** `lv_obj_t *` is `Obj`, a `Copy` generational handle into the
  `Ui` arena. Displays, input devices, groups, timers, animations, shared
  styles, layers, subjects and observers have their own handles (`DisplayId`,
  `IndevId`, `GroupId`, `TimerId`, `AnimId`, `StyleId`, `LayerId`,
  `SubjectId`, `ObserverId`). A handle of a deleted object is stale, not
  dangling: functions check it like `LV_CHECK_OBJ` and return what the C
  function returns for an invalid object.
- **Layer 1: `Ui` methods.** The functions of the object, style, event,
  display, input device, group, timer, animation, observer and draw modules
  are methods of `Ui` named after the C function without `lv_`, with the
  C object argument first: `lv_obj_set_width(obj, 100)` is
  `ui.obj_set_width(obj, 100)`, `lv_obj_add_style(obj, &s, sel)` is
  `ui.obj_add_style(obj, s, sel)`, `lv_timer_create(cb, period, ud)` is
  `ui.timer_create(cb, period, ud)`. The generated style setters also have
  short aliases (`ui.set_style_bg_color(obj, c, sel)`).
- **Layer 2: widget handles.** Every widget of `ferrovgl_widgets` is a `Copy`
  newtype over `Obj` whose methods take the `Ui` first:
  `lv_label_create(parent)` is `Label::create(&mut ui, parent)` and
  `lv_label_set_text(label, "Hi")` is `label.set_text(&mut ui, "Hi")`.
  `label.obj()` returns the base `Obj` for the layer-1 functions, and
  `Label::from_obj(&ui, obj)` checks the class of an existing object.
- **Values.** Styles, draw descriptors, areas and colours are plain Rust
  values: `lv_style_init(&s)` + `lv_style_set_bg_color(&s, c)` is
  `let mut s = Style::new(); s.set_bg_color(c);` (stored in the context with
  `ui.style_create(s)`, which returns the `StyleId`), and
  `lv_draw_rect_dsc_init(&d)` is `RectDsc::new()`. Pure helpers are free
  functions, e.g. `ferrovgl_core::misc::math::sqrt` for `lv_sqrt()`.
- **Callbacks** receive `&mut Ui`, so they may change or delete objects as in
  C: `lv_obj_add_event_cb(obj, cb, LV_EVENT_CLICKED, NULL)` is
  `ui.obj_add_event_cb(obj, Rc::new(|ui, e| { .. }), EventCode::CLICKED, None)`.
  Application state is stored with `ui.set_app(state)` and borrowed with
  `ui.app_mut::<T>()`.

```rust,ignore
let mut ui = Ui::new(UiConfig::default());          // lv_init()
ferrovgl_draw_sw::init(&mut ui);                    // lv_draw_sw_init()
let disp = ui.display_create(800, 480);             // lv_display_create(800, 480)
// ... ui.display_set_buffers(disp, ..) and ui.display_set_driver(disp, ..) ...
let screen = ui.screen_active().unwrap();           // lv_screen_active()
let label = Label::create(&mut ui, screen);         // lv_label_create(screen)
label.set_text(&mut ui, "Hello");                   // lv_label_set_text(label, "Hello")
ui.obj_center(label.obj());                         // lv_obj_center(label)
loop {
    ui.tick_inc(5);                                 // lv_tick_inc(5)
    ui.timer_handler();                             // lv_timer_handler()
}
```

## Reading the tables

Each upstream header under `include/lvgl/` has a table listing every public
`lv_*` function it declares (prototypes and `static inline` functions) and
every `#define lv_old lv_new` function alias (the old v8 and v9.x names of
`api_map/`), in header order.

- **mapped**: a public Rust item whose doc comment *starts* with the C
  name, e.g. `` /// `lv_obj_set_width()` ``. Several items can map one
  function (layer-1 method, alias, widget method). **mapped (deprecated)**:
  the function is deprecated upstream (`@deprecated`, `LV_DEPRECATED` or a
  leading `DEPRECATED`) or the Rust item is `#[deprecated]`.
- **crate-internal**: ported, but only as a `pub(crate)` or private item
  (not shown for a header excluded as a whole).
- **excluded**: not ported on purpose, with the reason (PLAN.md, deprecated
  upstream, or a C `va_list` variant). A deprecated alias lists the Rust
  items of the function it names: `lv_scr_act()` is `Ui::screen_active`.
- **not ported**: not available yet; the note says when it is planned or
  where the code explains the gap. `#if` conditions are the upstream ones.

The Rust feature in brackets is the `cfg` the item needs; a feature shared by
the whole table is given once above it. Run `cargo xtask gen-mapping` after
porting functions; `cargo xtask gen-mapping --check` (after
`cargo xtask refimgs sync`) fails when this page is out of date.
